intro.title: OAuth2 PKCE Flow in a SPA
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular Single Page Application (SPA) that securely authenticates users using the OAuth2 Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) flow. You will learn the core concept of OAuth2 authorization, which allows your app to request limited access to a user's data on another service without handling their password directly. The main technologies involved are Angular for the frontend framework, TypeScript for type-safe code, and the Angular HTTP client to communicate with an OAuth2 authorization server. By the end, you'll understand how to generate a code verifier and challenge, redirect users for login, and exchange an authorization code for an access token securely.
intro.usecase: The OAuth2 PKCE flow is essential for securing single-page applications that integrate with third-party services like Google, Microsoft, or GitHub. Developers implement this pattern when building dashboards that display authenticated user data, such as project management tools that sync with external APIs. For example, a financial analytics SPA might use PKCE to securely obtain tokens for accessing banking APIs, then display personalized charts and transaction panels. This flow ensures that sensitive user data remains protected while enabling seamless, interactive experiences in modern web applications.
